item.title: Chemical-Delithiation-Induced Surface Reconstruction in Layered Oxide Cathodes for High-Performance All-Solid-State Batteries
item.description:

Journal of the American Chemical Society | 🔬 Research Article
💡 Chemical delithiation with NO2BF4 reconstructs Li-rich layered oxide surfaces into a cation-disordered, fluorine-incorporating subsurface layer, passivating the oxidative interface and eliminating cathode–solid electrolyte degradation. This enables ~300.3 mAh g–1 capacity and 82.3% retention over 1500 cycles in all-solid-state batteries, and the strategy extends to Ni-rich oxides, offering a universal interfacial design route for high-energy ASSBs.

💡 This work introduces the first sulfonimide-based polymer of intrinsic microporosity (FAS-PIM) and directly compares it with flexible, non-microporous polysulfonimide analogs. 💡 This work introduces facet-induced electron-bridge engineering via a Mott–Schottky built-in electric field to enhance LiO₂-mediated kinetics in Li–O₂ batteries. The strategy offers a general principle for accelerating electron transfer and regulating intermediates through crystal-plane and interfacial engineering.

💡 This work introduces dual-functional CMC-Li supramolecular bridges linking PDA-modified LLZAO fillers in PVDF-HFP, simultaneously dispersing fillers and regulating ion solvation. The result is dendrite suppression, 1400 h cycling stability, and high-capacity retention, offering a generalizable paradigm for advanced composite solid electrolytes.

Advanced Functional Materials | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in a viscoelastic organic–inorganic solid electrolyte that converts free water to bound water, suppressing vanadium dissolution and stabilizing zinc anodes. Its significance is enabling ultra-stable vanadium-based zinc-ion batteries with 8500 h symmetric cycling and over 8000 cycles at 1.0 A g⁻¹, offering a practical “water confinement” strategy for durable energy storage.

item.title: Central‐Atom‐Differentiated Solvent Chemistry Enables Anion‐Reinforced Solvation for Ultra‐Long Cycling Ah‐Level Sodium‐Ion Pouch Cells
item.description:
افزودن ethylene sulfite به الکترولیت کربناته، سولواسیون تقویت‌شده با آنیون را ایجاد کرده و پوچ سل سدیم-یون با 81.29% ظرفیت پس از 3500 چرخه می‌سازد.
Advanced Materials | 🔬 Research Article
💡 Introducing ethylene sulfite into carbonate electrolytes differentiates solvent central-atom chemistry (sulfur vs. carbon), rebalancing solvent-anion competition to reinforce PF₆⁻ in Na⁺ solvation. This lowers desolvation barriers and forms inorganic-rich interphases on both electrodes, enabling a 2.34 Ah pouch cell to retain 81.29% capacity after 3500 cycles and operate from −20°C to 50°C.

Advanced Materials | 🔬 Research Article
💡 This work reframes PC co-intercalation in graphite as a system-level kinetic competition, not a fixed EC–PC disparity. It introduces the "lowest achievable potential" descriptor linking solvation, interphase, and operating conditions. Significance: a unified kinetic framework enabling rational electrolyte, binder, and graphite design to suppress solvent co-intercalation and stabilize graphite anodes.
